covered: ADR-0002 single DB engine vs in-process hosts

findings.claim: The single engine is node:sqlite, but OpenCode 2 (and Pi when run as its Bun-compiled binary) load the v2 plugin in-process under Bun. Bun 1.3.4 cannot resolve node:sqlite, so the in-process plugin cannot open context.db. v1 fixed this exact case with bun:sqlite (#45); PRD §12 removes 'Bun + bun:sqlite' with no replacement.
findings.evidence: Local: `bun bsq.mjs` (import {DatabaseSync} from 'node:sqlite') -> 'error: Could not resolve: "node:sqlite"' (bun 1.3.4). opencode@1438073 package.json:8 'packageManager: bun@1.4.2'; packages/cli/script/build.ts:153-170 Bun.build({compile:...}); packages/core/package.json:33-37 '#sqlite': bun -> sqlite.bun.ts, node -> sqlite.node.ts (OpenCode itself does not use node:sqlite under Bun). pi-mono packages/coding-agent/src/config.ts:21-25 isBunBinary/isBunRuntime; package.json:35 'bun build --compile'. PRD-v2.md:201 'Bun + bun:sqlite' removed; TECH-SPEC §3.7 Pi/OpenCode in-process.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: e4cf8a67 2026-03-19 'feat(sqlite): add bun:sqlite fallback adapter for Bun runtime (#45)'; 10f80b61 2026-03-21 'refactor: simplify SQLite driver selection — check globalThis.Bun first (#163)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'When better-sqlite3 is unavailable (Bun runtime), loadDatabase() now falls back to bun:sqlite'. REGRESSION_RISK: OpenCode 2/Pi-binary users get no store, journal, search or stats. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: no fallback chain at runtime; pick ONE engine per adapter row at build time.
findings.fix: Needs-decision in ADR-0002: either (a) plugin hosts never open the DB in-process and talk to the MCP server (one path), or (b) adapter table fixes the engine per host at build time (bun:sqlite for OpenCode 2 / Pi binary), not a runtime pick. Add S-BUN spike: live load of the plugin in OpenCode 2 and in the Pi binary.

findings.claim: S-NODE asks only for node:sqlite + timeout without a flag. It does not require FTS5. Some Node builds ship node:sqlite without FTS5; v1 probed for it and fell back to better-sqlite3. v2 has no second engine, so the docs must state the gate (minimum Node must ship FTS5) and the one-line hard error.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:392 '| S-NODE | Minimum Node version with `node:sqlite` + `timeout` and without a flag |'. v1 src/db-base.ts:192-196 'Some Node.js Linux builds (e.g. v22.14.0 on Ubuntu) ship node:sqlite without FTS5 ... silently breaks ctx_search'.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: a70b9c94 2026-05-07 'fix(db-base): probe FTS5 before adopting node:sqlite picker (#461) (#464)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'On Node builds whose bundled SQLite ships without FTS5 ... ctx_search / ctx_batch_execute / the doctor's FTS5 check silently break with "no such module: fts5"'. REGRESSION_RISK: silent search failure returns. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: no fallback to better-sqlite3 (removed); probe at DB open, hard error naming the Node upgrade.
findings.fix: Extend S-NODE to 'node:sqlite + timeout + FTS5 on macOS/Linux/Windows official builds and distro builds'; ADR-0002: FTS5 probe at open, missing -> one-line error; GP1 case on a Node without FTS5.

findings.claim: The project key is the git common dir, but no doc says how a hook process gets it. Each command hook is a fresh node fork; running git costs 12-50 ms, which alone breaks the 40 ms hook budget (GS6). v1 needed a tmpdir marker cache for this. v2 docs have no rule (cache, adapter-provided path, or read .git/commondir as a file).
findings.evidence: ADR-0002:17 '~/.context-mode/projects/<git-common-dir-hash>/context.db'; TECH-SPEC.md:39 GS6 p95 <= 40 ms; v1 hooks/session-helpers.mjs:60-63 'every Pre/PostToolUse hook is a fresh node fork ... lets subsequent forks short-circuit the 12-50ms git worktree list cost'; src/session/db.ts:304-305 '~12ms (git worktree list subprocess fork) on macOS, 50ms+ on Windows'.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 61fd3fb0 2026-05-09 'Fix worktree suffix project root detection (#435)'; da6b117a 2026-05-10 'refactor(hooks): bind session-helpers to bundled TS'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: comment above. REGRESSION_RISK: hook latency and Windows timeouts return. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: no spawn per hook; one method, no git-then-cwd chain.
findings.fix: ADR-0002: compute the key without a subprocess (read `.git` file / `commondir` file, realpath, case-fold rule) in one function shared by server and hooks; GP3 bench asserts no child process in the hook.

findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:137 'Runtimes found by PATH lookup'; v1 src/runtime.ts:130,147 'if (commandExists("bun")) return "bun"'; TECH-SPEC.md:98 Bun text removed as machine-dependent.
